topic: NEER and REER: measuring the rupee against a weighted basket of currencies, with and without inflation

concepts.name: CPI and WPI as the model
concepts.prereq_recalled: inflation videos: a basket of goods and a weighted average of price changes

concepts.name: reading NEER (appreciation / depreciation)
concepts.prereq_recalled: NEER as units of the basket per rupee

concepts.name: REER
concepts.prereq_recalled: NEER method with one column changed

book_understanding.teaching_order: A textbook would define NEER and REER and give their formulas. This video starts from everyday prices moving unequally, recalls how CPI and WPI answer 'is inflation rising?', and mirrors that question for the currency, so NEER and REER arrive as the expected answer. NEER is then built as a worked table, REER as one extra column on the same table, and a comparison with a memory rule closes it.
book_understanding.breakdown_rule: Teach the new pair through a known pair (CPI/WPI), then build the first index as a worked table and the second as one change to that table.

opening.what: A grid of everyday items with price arrows flickering up and down while the voice says prices never all move together; then it asks how you would tell whether inflation is rising.

moves.concept: CPI and WPI as the model
moves.what: Prices of different things keep moving; some rise while others fall, and later it may flip.

moves.concept: CPI and WPI as the model
moves.what: If I asked you whether mahangai is rising or falling, how would you tell?

moves.concept: CPI and WPI as the model
moves.what: With two indexes: CPI yaani consumer price index, WPI yaani wholesale price index.

moves.concept: CPI and WPI as the model
moves.what: Each uses its own basket; the index is a weighted average of the basket's price changes.
Jis tarah two indexes tell us about inflation, bilkul usi tarah two indexes tell us whether our currency is appreciating or depreciating against others.
NEER yaani nominal effective exchange rate; REER yaani real effective exchange rate.
We trade with many countries, the rupee's rate with each keeps changing, tracking each is impossible, so we need one index.
Take a basket of the currencies we trade with most, weight each by trade volume, multiply each rupee rate by its weight and add: that total is NEER.
Another way to see it: the rupee's rate against the whole basket.
If NEER rises over time the rupee is appreciating against its main partners; if it falls, depreciating.
So that was NEER, yaani nominal effective exchange rate.
If we make one small change in the same calculation: add a column for the real exchange rate.
A country's exchange rate adjusted for inflation is the real exchange rate; the formula is shown.
Use real rates instead of nominal ones in the same sum, and the result is REER.
NEER is the weighted average of the rupee's rates against major partners; adding each country's inflation gives REER.
'Yaad rakhiye' rule: if the rupee's REER is above its NEER, India's inflation is higher than its major partners'.

examples.what: Icons of a house, food, a bus, medicine, fuel and more, whose price arrows keep flipping up and down.
examples.carries: prices move unequally, so one index is needed

examples.what: The inflation question answered by two indexes, set above the currency question answered by two indexes.
India trades with many countries, so the rupee has many exchange rates at once (globe sending arrows into India).
Six currencies weighted 30/20/20/10/10/10, each rupee rate multiplied by its weight and summed to 0.26849 (on screen only, never read aloud).

closing.what: A 'remember this' rule (REER above NEER means higher inflation at home) on a '<' sign, under a promo; no REER number is ever worked out.

narration.density: About 10 terms (CPI, WPI, weighted average, NEER, REER, basket of currencies, weight, nominal and real exchange rate, appreciate / depreciate) in about 235 s, about 2.5 per minute. The analogy keeps it light, but the table numbers go by unspoken.

talmel_summary: In the NEER part the picture walks the calculation step by step on the same words (weight, rate, multiply, add), but the actual numbers are on screen only and never read. The analogy panel (inflation question above the currency question) is the strongest fit of speech and picture. REER gets a column that is never filled, and the closing rule is a '<' sign plus text, so the picture stops showing meaning exactly where the new idea arrives.

voice.notes: About 210 words per minute, the fastest of this batch; confident and flowing. Every acronym is unpacked with 'yaani'. NEER and REER are said 'neer' / 'reer' (recognised as 'near', 'rear', 'NIR'). Table numbers are not read. Short pauses (about 0.6-0.7 s) only around the CPI / WPI unpacking. Closes with 'yaad rakhiye'.

game_ideas.player_does: Sets trade weights for six partner currencies (must total 100%), then sees one month's exchange-rate moves and calls whether the rupee appreciated or depreciated; in level two, switches on each country's inflation.
game_ideas.process_happens: The table multiplies and adds live and shows NEER and its change; in level two the REAL column fills, REER appears beside NEER, and the rupee coin grows or shrinks against the basket.
game_ideas.win: Correct appreciation / depreciation calls for five months, and a correct prediction of whether REER ends above or below NEER.
game_ideas.lose: Weights not adding to 100% lock the sum; calling 'appreciated' when NEER fell shows the rupee coin shrinking against the basket; ignoring inflation shows REER drifting away from NEER.
game_ideas.concept: NEER calculation, its reading, and REER

game_ideas.player_does: Matches parts of the inflation toolkit to their currency twins: basket of goods to basket of currencies, price change to exchange-rate change, consumption weight to trade weight, CPI/WPI question to NEER/REER question.
game_ideas.process_happens: Each correct pair lights up both panels side by side, as in the video's mirrored layout.
game_ideas.lose: Pairing 'basket of goods' with 'inflation adjustment' shows the mismatch: the currency basket holds currencies weighted by trade.
game_ideas.concept: need for a currency index (analogy with CPI/WPI)

checks_learned: When a worked table gains a column for a second method, the column must be filled and the new total shown (here the REAL column stays empty and no REER number appears).
Numbers in a worked example must be read aloud or pointed at at least once (walk the first row: 30% of 0.012 gives 0.0036).
A formula shown on screen must be read once, or walked with one substitution.
A 'remember this' rule (REER above NEER means higher inflation) needs its reason in one spoken line or a picture; a bare '<' sign fails.
A new concept that mirrors an old one should be shown side by side with it in the same structure; this video's CPI/WPI to NEER/REER panel is the model.

teaching_best.why: Analogy bridge: the known inflation question and its two indexes sit above the new currency question, so the learner expects two indexes before they are named.
The cause chain (many partners, many rates, cannot track each, need one index) gives the reason for the index before its method.
REER is taught as 'one small change' to the NEER table, so the second method costs only one new idea.

teaching_weak.why: REER is never computed: the real-rate column stays empty and no REER value appears.
The closing rule (REER above NEER) comes with no reason and no example.
The worked NEER numbers are on screen only; the voice describes the steps in general words.
